12K views · 78 reactions | Why Vietnam Is Stuck Between America And China
Vietnam has about 100 million people, with China to the north and the South China Sea to the east. China is its biggest trading partner, with $256 billion in trade in 2025, up 25%. Vietnam buys parts and materials from China, assembles them, and ships the finished goods to America, its biggest export market. Cut either line, and Vietnam’s factories feel it. Washington sees Chinese goods being routed through Vietnam to dodge tariffs, which Vietnam says it does not tolerate. In July 2026, America added a 12.5% tariff on Vietnamese goods, while a trade deal is still in its final stages with no signing date. In April 2026, Vietnam’s To Lam made his first foreign trip as president to Beijing and called China a strategic priority. Yet Vietnam has the most direct territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea, so it hedges, with a free trade deal with the EU and CPTPP membership. This map breakdown explains why Vietnam isn’t choosing between America and China. It sells to one and buys from the other.
